draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Hospet! The great Vijayanagara ruler Krishna Deva Raya founded this town in honour of his mother Nagamma, and today it's the gateway to Hampi, just 13 km away.
draft.hungryLine: I don't have a named place to eat in my notes for Hospet, so ask a local where they go for a meal.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Madina Masjid is a 6 min walk and Kaalammana Gudi is about 8 minutes away. For the big ruins, Hampi is 13 km from town.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Head down to the banks of the Tungabhadra River and watch the water go by.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Hospet is known as the steel city of Karnataka, and it's the largest and fastest-growing industrial city in Vijayanagara district.

tips.title: Use Hospet as your Hampi base.
tips.body: The UNESCO-listed ruins are just 13 km away, so it's an easy trip out and back.

tips.title: Break up long road trips here.
tips.body: Hospet is the link between North and South Karnataka, 333 km from Bengaluru.

story.title: An empire next door
story.body: Just up the road, Hampi was once the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire. Today those ruins are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

story.title: A town for a mother
story.body: The Vijayanagara ruler Krishna Deva Raya founded Hospet in honour of his mother, Nagamma. He set it on the banks of the Tungabhadra River.

story.title: The steel city
story.body: Hospet, officially Hosapete, is now the headquarters of Vijayanagara district and its biggest industrial city. People call it the steel city of Karnataka.
